headline: A 'Lol' Tweet, a French Wafermaker, and a 517% Year
lede: @aleabitoreddit greets a 517% year-to-date gain in Soitec, a Grenoble-based maker of engineered semiconductor wafers, with a single line: "I might be pretty good at this? $SOI up enormous amounts lol." The casualness obscures a more serious story about how the AI build-out has begun to grope past silicon and into the substrate beneath it.
body:
Soitec SA, listed on Euronext Paris under the ticker SOI, does not design chips. It does not run a foundry. It supplies engineered wafers — the polished discs of crystalline material on which others etch transistors. Its flagship product is silicon-on-insulator, or SOI: a wafer in which a thin layer of silicon (around 220 nanometers, for the photonics grade) sits atop a buried layer of oxide, which sits atop a thicker silicon handle. The oxide electrically isolates the working silicon above, which reduces leakage currents, allows lower-power switching, and, crucially, traps light. Soitec's proprietary 'Smart Cut' process — hydrogen-ion implantation followed by thermal cleaving — has been refined for three decades and sits behind roughly 4,300 patents. Bank of America estimates Soitec's share of the photonics-grade SOI market at over 95%.

Until recently, this was a quiet, cyclical business. Most of Soitec's revenue came from RF-SOI wafers used in 5G smartphone radios, a market that has been working through pandemic-era oversupply. The stock had lost around three-quarters of its value over five years; the second OCR'd chart in the bookmark, showing the share price at 44.17 EUR and down 72.75% over five years, captures that earlier mood. By March 9, 2026, shares bottomed at 41.77 EUR.

What changed was the conversation about co-packaged optics, or CPO — the architecture in which optical transceivers (the components that convert electrical signals into light pulses) are mounted directly onto the same package as a network switch or GPU rather than sitting in a pluggable module across the board. CPO promises to break the so-called copper wall: at the bandwidths AI clusters now require, electrical interconnects between chips burn too much power and run too hot. Light is cheaper. Building optical engines at scale, however, requires photonic integrated circuits, and those are fabricated almost exclusively on photonics-grade SOI wafers — Soitec's wafers.

The market began to notice this in March, after NVIDIA's GTC conference featured CPO prominently in roadmaps for Spectrum-X switches and future GPU packages. Citigroup raised its Soitec price target by nearly 50% on April 10, when the stock jumped 19% in a single session. Oddo BHF lifted its target to 85 EUR from 50; Deutsche Bank followed. By April 17, Bloomberg had labelled Soitec the best-performing European stock of 2026. The chart in the tweet shows it at 153.55 EUR on May 4, up 517.41% YTD, with a market capitalization of 5.29 billion EUR. A separate intraday wire that day put the move at +30.8% in a single session.

This is not, strictly speaking, an earnings-driven rally. Revenue declined roughly 10% year-over-year in the most recent reporting period; Soitec's photonics segment is still only around 100 million EUR of annual sales, dwarfed by mobile. The company's full-year results are scheduled for May 27. What the market has done is re-rate Soitec from a tired smartphone supplier into the substrate monopolist for an architecture that NVIDIA has telegraphed as central to its Feynman-generation systems. The price-to-earnings ratio now sits near 394, against a European semiconductor sector average around 29.

As for the poster: Serenity, the account behind @aleabitoreddit, was not on this trade by accident. Their public posts show them taking a 'sizable position' in Soitec around 43 EUR in early March, ahead of GTC, on the explicit thesis that Soitec was a 'genuine monopoly' on CPO substrates trading at one times book. The 'lol' is, in that light, slightly less casual than it reads.

concepts.definition: A wafer architecture in which a thin layer of crystalline silicon sits atop a buried layer of insulating oxide, which itself sits on a silicon handle wafer. The oxide electrically isolates the working silicon above, reducing leakage currents and parasitic capacitance and, in the photonics variant, confining light so it can travel through the silicon as a waveguide.

A specialized SOI process in which the top silicon layer is so thin that the transistor channel is fully depleted of charge carriers when off. The result is high speed at very low operating voltages, which is why FD-SOI shows up in mmWave-capable iPhones, Wi-Fi 7 modems, and Starlink satellite radios.

An SOI wafer engineered to extreme uniformity (silicon thickness held within roughly one nanometer across the wafer, defect density below 0.1 per square centimeter) so that light can be guided losslessly through patterned silicon waveguides. It is the foundation substrate for silicon photonic integrated circuits.

Soitec's proprietary process for manufacturing SOI wafers. Hydrogen ions are implanted at a precise depth in a silicon donor wafer, which is then bonded to an oxidized handle wafer; thermal treatment cleaves the donor along the implant plane, leaving a thin, atomically uniform layer of silicon on the oxide. Roughly 4,300 patents protect the technique.

A data-center architecture in which optical transceivers — the components that convert electrical signals into light — are integrated directly onto the same package as a network switch ASIC or, eventually, a GPU. By moving the optics in close, CPO sidesteps the power and bandwidth limits of long copper traces and pluggable optical modules.

The discipline of building optical components — waveguides, modulators, detectors — using the same lithographic processes as silicon CMOS chips. Crucially, these circuits require an SOI substrate to confine light in the silicon layer.

An SOI variant optimized for radio-frequency switches and front-end modules in cellular phones. Soitec holds a roughly 70%+ share of this market; it was the company's largest revenue line for years and is the segment whose post-pandemic glut depressed the stock through 2024–25.

fact_check: The 517.41% YTD figure shown in the tweet's image (Soitec at 153.55 EUR on May 4, 2026) is consistent with public reporting. Bloomberg via Moneyweb had Soitec up roughly 270% YTD as of April 18; a separate intraday wire on May 4 put the stock up 30.8% in a single session to 147.95 EUR, with YTD at 447%. The 153.55 close and 517% figure imply further intraday strength on May 4 and are consistent with the stock's documented melt-up. The 41.77 EUR low on March 9 also matches contemporary reporting. The company is genuinely Paris-listed under SOI; market capitalization of around 5.29 billion EUR is plausible at that share price.
